02 Before / After

A daily reading list should not start with five tabs

The job is not to create more tabs. It is to create a candidate list that takes you back to the original source. The friction is the manual work of turning scattered leads into a readable list.

01

Collecting leads

Open papers, repositories, and community pages separately, then copy them into a personal list.

02

Removing repeats

The same link can appear in multiple places and must be compared manually.

03

Seeing gaps

When a source is missing, it is difficult to know why.

05 Solution

From topics to a readable briefing

Set the themes and time window. Add the links already found. The Skill fetches available sources, merges, deduplicates, ranks, and returns items with source status.

InputTopics, window, limits, supplied links
ProcessFetch, merge, deduplicate, rank
OutputDigest, structured items, source status

X, Xiaohongshu, and Google are supplied by the calling Agent through extra_items; the Skill does not fetch them directly.

06 Standard use case

Standard use case: a daily AI briefing

Set topics such as AI, LLM, and machine learning for the past 24 hours. The Skill gathers papers, open-source projects, and community activity into a linked candidate reading list.

We ran the English standard prompt live: past 24 hours, up to five items per source, with no extra_items supplied. The run returned 10 candidate entries: 5 from GitHub and 5 from Hacker News.

This turns scattered sources into one traceable starting point, from which research, product, or editorial teams can decide what deserves follow-up.

Note: candidate lists can include irrelevant items. Editorial review remains necessary.

Stability

Stability: repeated news stays once

When the same link comes from multiple sources, the Skill deduplicates it through normalized URLs or similar titles, reducing manual comparison.

Deduplication uses normalized URLs or similar titles. Source order affects the retained item, and the Skill does not fuse multiple summaries into a new claim.

Verifiability

Verifiability: replay the same processing offline

The supplied fixture covers duplicates, empty summaries, and simulated source failures, so the processing rules can be checked repeatedly.

For stable reproduction, pin now or supply a fixture with a valid reference time. Network-source failures degrade to unavailable status; invalid inputs still return structured errors.

Test data, not current-news evidence.

07 / 08

Make collection a reusable reading starting point

The Skill does not decide whether a paper is reliable, a project is mature, or a discussion deserves attention. It gathers the inputs for that judgment into a linked list.

“Each retained item carries a source link, and an unavailable source remains visible in the result.”
